description:
Building an intuitive tool for mission planners, educators, and the public to compare lunar landing sites and dates at a glance by visualizing Sun and Earth positions above the real terrain horizon to reveal power and communication windows.

Our team lead is an NJIT engineering student, team lead of a NASA ORBIT Challenge finalist for a space-based solar power concept, and the PI of a NASA-funded lunar robotics project, so we know why these windows make or break a mission.

Anyone welcome!
summary: A user-friendly program that compares and scores different landing sites by terrain slope (LOLA slope), surface composition (Lunar Prospector Iron and Titanium) , direct-to-Earth contact (Earth visibility), illumination and proximity to permanently shadowed regions where ice may be found (NASA Lunar Polar Illumination, LOLA), data while taking into account how the date and time affects the site’s characteristics. The user controls the ranking system by altering the ‘grading rubric’ to suit their mission/research needs and priorities. Our goal is for SLSI to become a tool for professional researchers, mission planners, amateurs, classrooms and the general science community to explore the lunar surface and understand how it affects their missions and technology. Sunlit Summit’s personal goal is to rank regions of the South pole by their concentrations of iron and titanium, for possible sites for research into  combustion synthesis research, which burns mixed moon dirt with metal powder to turn regolith into dense ceramic, we could have “in-house” building bricks for landing pads, shelters and more. Bringing the necessary materials to the moon to build a permanent lunar base is very hard and expensive, this could be the solution that moves forward our efforts for a permanent lunar presence.
